newsitem.title: UK: Exco slides after H1 results disappoint.
newsitem.headline: Exco slides after H1 results disappoint.

text.p: Shares in Exco Plc slipped on Tuesday after the money and bonds broker posted a fall in pretax profits and predicted a gloomy outlook for the rest of the year, traders said.
Shares slid 15 1/2 p to 71 1/2p by 0815 GMT.

Exco said pre-tax profit fell to 12.1 million stg in the six months to June 30 from 16.1 million stg in the previous year. The company halved its interim dividend to 1.5p from 3.0p in the previous year.
"The results were very disappointing," said one analyst.

Analysts recalled that in March the company had said they were happy with the current level of dividend. "But now they've halved the interim dividend and said that given the outlook for the full year they can't be optimistic," said one analyst.

Exco said there was little evidence to suggest an improvement in volumes and revenues in the remaining months of the year and it was "probable" that it would also recommend a halving of the final dividend.
Many analysts said they would now be downgrading their forecasts for full year results.
"Given that full year results are weighted towards the first half, I'm going to be revising full year estimates from around 25 million stg to 20 million stg," said one analyst.

Analysts said they were encouraged by Exco's plans to shift the mix of business from foreign exchange towards securities and derivatives. "Foreign exchange broking has been hit heavily by the electronic matching systems," an analyst said.
A seven million stg reduction in the group's costs base compared to the same period last year, and continued efforts to cut and control costs were also encouraging, they added.
